reading.body:
This facility at 32 Avenue of the Americas in Manhattan is a historic carrier hotel operated by Digital Realty within its New York/New Jersey metro hub. Digital Realty does not publish an IT power capacity figure for this building on its property page or in its financial filings, which disclose portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than by individual asset. Its operator publishes aggregate capacity across 310 global data centers in more than 55 metros, but not building-by-building power ratings, so the scale of this specific facility's AI infrastructure potential cannot be read from public data.

The building sits in a region where two utilities serve the metro: Con Edison covers most of Manhattan, and PSE&G covers most of northern New Jersey. New York and New Jersey have both faced growing regulatory and community scrutiny around data center siting and grid interconnection, a constraint that applies to this facility alongside the region's established role as a dense financial and network hub. Thirty-one facilities are mapped across New York state in this registry, but only one publishes a megawatt capacity figure, totaling 3 MW, so this campus ranks second by disclosed power among mapped facilities in the state, a ranking that reflects the absence of published data more than deployed capacity.

Digital Realty operates as a colocation landlord rather than a compute operator, meaning this facility hosts hyperscaler and enterprise tenants rather than serving as the company's own training or inference platform. Without published power or square footage for this address, the decision to treat it as material to AI scaling depends on whether tenant operators choose to concentrate accelerator density here, a choice not disclosed in operator specifications and not visible from the outside.
